name: Mona

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mona is another name for Anglesey, a British and Welsh sacred island. The Roman historian Tacitus described a Druid sanctuary on it. Roman soldiers destroyed that sanctuary around 59 to 64 CE. Druids ran a college on the island. Celtic women priestesses, robed in black, screamed like the raven-goddess Mórrígan while the priests fought. Romans had already cut sacred groves and massacred clergy in other Celtic lands. The druids of Anglesey knew what fate awaited their houses and their honored trees. The druids died in battle or were executed, and the great forests burned. Bogs and lakes on Anglesey later yielded troves in Celtic design. The Druids likely hid them during the invasion. The island may have been sacred before the Celts, since an ancient cairn sits atop the hill of Bryn-Celli-Dhu. Diana Paxson depicted the destruction in her Arthurian trilogy.
objective: Document the sacred island of Mona, also known as Anglesey.
